sentences.text: A century ago, the immigrants from across the Atlantic included settlers and sojourners.

sentences.text: Along with the many folks looking to make a permanent home in the United States came those who had no intention to stay, and who would make some money and then go home.
Between 1908 and 1915, about 7 million people arrived while about 2 million departed.
About a quarter of all Italian immigrants, for example, eventually returned to Italy for good.
They even had an affectionate nickname, "uccelli di passaggio," birds of passage.
Today, we are much more rigid about immigrants.

sentences.text: We divide newcomers into two categories: legal or illegal, good or bad.
We hail them as Americans in the making, or brand them as aliens to be kicked out.
That framework has contributed mightily to our broken immigration system and the long political paralysis over how to fix it.
We don't need more categories, but we need to change the way we think about categories.
We need to look beyond strict definitions of legal and illegal.
To start, we can recognize the new birds of passage, those living and thriving in the gray areas.
We might then begin to solve our immigration challenges.
Crop pickers, violinists, construction workers, entrepreneurs, engineers, home health-care aides and physicists are among today's birds of passage.

sentences.text: They are energetic participants in a global economy driven by the flow of work, money and ideas.

sentences.text: We need them to imagine the United States as a place where they can be productive for a while without committing themselves to staying forever.

sentences.translation: 科学家发现，尽管我们容易做出过激的本能反应，但如果我们花一点时间思考自己可能会如何反应，就能减少甚至消除这种快速的、与生俱来的反应所带来的负面影响。

sentences.text: Snap decisions can be important defense mechanisms; if we are judging whether someone is dangerous, our brains and bodies are hard-wired to react very quickly, within milliseconds.
sentences.translation: 快速决策可能是重要的防御机制；如果我们在判断某人是否危险时，我们的大脑和身体会在几毫秒内做出非常迅速的本能反应。但我们需要更多时间来评估其他因素。研究表明，要准确判断某人是否善于社交，我们至少需要一分钟，最好是五分钟。判断性格中的复杂方面，如神经质或开放性，需要一段时间。

sentences.text: When Dr. Gottman really wants to assess whether a couple will stay together, he invites them to his island retreat for a much longer evaluation: two days, not two seconds.

sentences.translation: 我们通过暂停来抑制与生俱来的反应的能力，正是我们与动物的区别所在：狗只能间歇性地或在几分钟内思考未来。但从历史上看，我们每天大约有百分之十二的时间在思考长远问题。尽管技术可能会改变我们的反应方式，但它并没有改变我们的本性。我们仍然拥有超越诱惑、扭转高速趋势的想象力。

sentences.text: But historically we have spent about 12 percent of our days contemplating the longer term.

translation.content:
P1 I can pick a date from the past 53 years and know instantly where I was, what happened in the
news and even the day of the week. I've been able to do this since I was four.
P2 I never feel overwhelmed with the amount of information my brain absorbs. My mind seems to
be able to cope and the information is stored away neatly. When I think of a sad memory, I do what
everybody does – try to put it to one side. I don't think it's harder for me just because my memory is
clearer. Powerful memory doesn't make my emotions any more acute or vivid. I can recall the day my
grandfather died and the sadness I felt when we went to the hospital the day before. I also remember
that the musical play Hair opened on Broadway on the same day – they both just pop into my mind in
the same way.

那天是星期几。自四岁起，我就一直能这样。
P2 我从不觉得大脑所吸收的海量信息会让我招架不住。我的头脑似乎应付得来，各种信息都被整

因为我的记忆更清晰，这件事对我而言就更难。超强的记忆并不会让我的情绪变得更加强烈或鲜明。
我能回忆起外公去世的那天，以及前一天我们去医院时我所感到的悲伤；我也记得，音乐剧《长发》

Section II Part A (2)
Directions:
Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark
your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
Text 2
P1 A century ago, the immigrants from across the Atlantic included settlers and sojourners. Along
with the many folks looking to make a permanent home in the United States came those who had no
intention to stay, and who would make some money and then go home. Between 1908 and 1915, about
7 million people arrived while about 2 million departed. About a quarter of all Italian immigrants, for
example, eventually returned to Italy for good. They even had an affectionate nickname, "uccelli di
passaggio," birds of passage.
一个世纪前，来自大西洋彼岸的移民包括定居者和旅居者。在许多希望在美国永久定居的人当中，也有那
些无意久留、赚些钱后就回国的人。1908年至1915年间，约有700万人抵达美国,而约有200万人离开。
例如，大约四分之一的意大利移民最终永久返回了意大利。他们甚至有一个亲切的昵称——"uccelli di
passaggio",即过境之鸟。
P2 Today, we are much more rigid about immigrants. We divide newcomers into two categories:
legal or illegal, good or bad. We hail them as Americans in the making, or brand them as aliens to be
kicked out. That framework has contributed mightily to our broken immigration system and the long
political paralysis over how to fix it. We don't need more categories, but we need to change the way we
think about categories. We need to look beyond strict definitions of legal and illegal. To start, we can
recognize the new birds of passage, those living and thriving in the gray areas. We might then begin to
solve our immigration challenges.
今天,我们对移民的态度要严格得多。我们将新来者分为两类：合法或非法,好或坏。我们把他们誉为未来
的美国人,或把他们打上外来者的烙印予以驱逐。这种框架极大地导致了我们破碎的移民制度以及在如何修
复这一问题上长期的政治僵局。我们不需要更多的分类,但我们需要改变思考分类的方式。我们需要超越合

P3 Crop pickers, violinists, construction workers, entrepreneurs, engineers, home health-care aides
and physicists are among today's birds of passage. They are energetic participants in a global economy
driven by the flow of work, money and ideas. They prefer to come and go as opportunity calls them.
They can manage to have a job in one place and a family in another.

P5 Accommodating this new world of people in motion will require new attitudes on both sides of

Section II Part A (3)
Directions:
Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark
your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
Text 3
P1 Scientists have found that although we are prone to snap overreactions, if we take a moment
and think about how we are likely to react, we can reduce or even eliminate the negative effects of our
quick, hard-wired responses.
科学家发现，尽管我们容易做出过激的本能反应，但如果我们花一点时间思考自己可能会如何反应，就能
减少甚至消除这种快速的、与生俱来的反应所带来的负面影响。
P2 Snap decisions can be important defense mechanisms; if we are judging whether someone is
dangerous, our brains and bodies are hard-wired to react very quickly, within milliseconds. But we need
more time to assess other factors. To accurately tell whether someone is sociable, studies show, we need
at least a minute, preferably five. It takes a while to judge complex aspects of personality, like
neuroticism or open-mindedness.
快速决策可能是重要的防御机制；如果我们在判断某人是否危险时，我们的大脑和身体会在几毫秒内做出
非常迅速的本能反应。但我们需要更多时间来评估其他因素。研究表明，要准确判断某人是否善于社交，
我们至少需要一分钟，最好是五分钟。判断性格中的复杂方面，如神经质或开放性，需要一段时间。
P3 But snap decisions in reaction to rapid stimuli aren't exclusive to the interpersonal realm.
Psychologists at the University of Toronto found that viewing a fast-food logo for just a few
milliseconds primes us to read 20 percent faster, even though reading has little to do with eating. We
unconsciously associate fast food with speed and impatience and carry those impulses into whatever else
we're doing, Subjects exposed to fast-food flashes also tend to think a musical piece lasts too long.
但对快速刺激做出的本能决策并不仅限于人际领域。多伦多大学的心理学家发现，仅仅看几毫秒的快餐标
志就会促使我们的阅读速度提高百分之二十，尽管阅读与进食几乎没有关系。我们会无意识地将快餐与速

P4 Yet we can reverse such influences. If we know we will overreact to consumer products or
housing options when we see a happy face (one reason good sales representatives and real estate agents
are always smiling), we can take a moment before buying. If we know female job screeners are more
likely to reject attractive female applicants, we can help screeners understand their biases – or hire
outside screeners.
然而我们可以扭转这种影响。如果我们知道当看到笑脸时会对消费品或住房选择反应过度（这是优秀销售

人员。
P5 John Gottman, the marriage expert, explains that we quickly "thin slice" information reliably
only after we ground such snap reactions in "thick sliced" long-term study. When Dr. Gottman really
wants to assess whether a couple will stay together, he invites them to his island retreat for a much
longer evaluation: two days, not two seconds.
婚姻专家John Gottman解释说，只有在我们将这种快速反应建立在"厚切片"式的长期研究基础上之后，
我们才能可靠地快速"薄切片"信息。当Gottman博士真正想要评估一对夫妇是否会在一起时，他会邀请他
们到他的岛屿静修所进行更长时间的评估：两天，而不是两秒钟。
P6 Our ability to mute our hard-wired reactions by pausing is what differentiates us from animals:
dogs can think about the future only intermittently or for a few minutes. But historically we have spent
about 12 percent of our days contemplating the longer term. Although technology might change the way
we react, it hasn't changed our nature. We still have the imaginative capacity to rise above temptation
and reverse the high-speed trend.
我们通过暂停来抑制与生俱来的反应的能力，正是我们与动物的区别所在：狗只能间歇性地或在几分钟内

的反应方式，但它并没有改变我们的本性。我们仍然拥有超越诱惑、扭转高速趋势的想象力。

【判型】The time needed in making decisions may____. 没有 infer/imply/mainly about 这类
提示词，只是要补全「决策所需时间会怎么样」这一具体特征，属于针对原文某句话的细节
考查。
【拆句】The time needed in making decisions may____. 主干是 The time may ____.，needed
in making decisions 是过去分词短语作后置定语修饰 The time，等价于 which is needed
in making decisions；空格处补一个动词原形作谓语。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
【定位】Snap decisions can be important defense mechanisms; if we are judging whether someone is
dangerous, our brains and bodies are hard-wired to react very quickly, within milliseconds.
But we need more time to assess other factors. To accurately tell whether someone is
sociable, studies show, we need at least a minute, preferably five. It takes a while to judge
complex aspects of personality, like neuroticism or open-mindedness.
快速决策可以是重要的防御机制；如果判断的是某人是否危险，我们的大脑和身体被天生设
定为在毫秒内迅速反应。但要评估其他因素，我们就需要更多时间：要准确判断一个人是否
合群，研究显示至少需要 1 分钟、最好 5 分钟；判断神经质或心胸开放等复杂人格特质则需
更久。
【选项】A) 过度推断
原文从未说决策时间决定（predetermine）判断准确性；段内只说「需要更多时间才能
accurately tell」，是「足够时间是准确的必要条件」而非「时间预先决定准确性」。
B) 答非所问
题干问的是「时间会怎么样」，B 项 prove the complexity of our brain reaction 谈的
是「证明大脑反应的复杂性」，把答案焦点从「时间」偷换成「大脑反应的属性」，没
有回答题干。
C) 偷换概念
原文谈「是否危险」是 defense mechanisms（防御机制需要快），用「紧迫」一词更
贴切；选项 the importance of the assessment 把「紧迫程度」偷换成「评估的重要
性」——很多判断重要却不紧迫（比如评估复杂人格其实很重要，但反而需要更多时
间），与原文事实相反。
D) ✓ 正确
if we are judging whether someone is dangerous, our brains and bodies are hard-wired to react
very quickly, within milliseconds
↔ vary according to the urgency of the situation
within milliseconds、at least a minute, preferably five、a while ↔ vary
预判说所需时间随被判断事项不同而不同；D 选项把「不同事项」抽象为「不同

[ A ]critical assessment
[ B ]"thin sliced" study
[ C ]adequate information
[ D ]sensible explanation
John Gottman认为可靠的快速反应基于____。
A) 批判性评估 B) "薄片式"研究 C) 充分的信息 D) 合理的解释
【答案】C （细节题）
【判型】John Gottman says that reliable snap reactions are based on____. 直接转述 Gottman
的原话观点，是观点细节题，不是推断或主旨。
【拆句】John Gottman says that reliable snap reactions are based on____. 主干 John Gottman
says that...；that 引导宾语从句，从句中 are based on 是被动结构，空格处补名词短语作
on 的宾语。无陷阱。
【定位】John Gottman, the marriage expert, explains that we quickly "thin slice" information reliably
only after we ground such snap reactions in "thick sliced" long-term study.
婚姻专家约翰·戈特曼解释说：只有当我们把这种快速反应建立在「厚切」长期研究的基础上
之后，「薄切」式的快速信息处理才会变得可靠。
【选项】A) 无中生有
原文谈的是「先做长期研究、积累信息」，从未谈 critical assessment（批判性评
估）；Gottman 的方法是「时间投入」而非「批判性评估」。
B) 与原文相反
Gottman 原句是 only after we ground such snap reactions in "thick sliced" long-
term study——快速反应（thin slice）要可靠，须建立在 thick sliced（厚切）研究之
上，「基础是 thick sliced」；B 项 "thin sliced" study 反过来说基础是 thin sliced，
恰好与原文相反。
C) ✓ 正确
we ground such snap reactions in "thick sliced" long-term study ↔ adequate information
two days, not two seconds ↔ adequate information
预判强调「足量＋长期的信息积累」，C 项用 adequate information（充分的信息）一
次性覆盖这两个语义，正面命中。
D) 无中生有
原文谈的是「研究」「长期评估」，从未谈 sensible explanation（合理的解释）；
Gottman 谈的是数据/观察过程，不是「解释」。

Section II Part B
Directions:
Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subheading from the list
A-G for each of the numbered paragraphs (41-45). There are two extra subheadings which you do not
need to use. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
The hugely popular blog the Skint Foodie chronicles how Tony balances his love of good food with
living on benefits. After bills, Tony has £60 a week to spend, £40 of which goes on food, but 10 years
ago he was earning £130,000 a year working in corporate communications and eating at London's best
restaurants at least twice a week. Then his marriage failed, his career burned out and his drinking
became serious. "The community mental health team saved my life. And I felt like that again, to a
certain degree, when people responded to the blog so well. It gave me the validation and confidence that
I'd lost. But it's still a day-by-day thing." Now he's living in a council flat and fielding offers from
literary agents. He's feeling positive, but he'll carry on blogging – not about eating as cheaply as you
can – "there are so many people in a much worse state, with barely any money to spend on food" – but
eating well on a budget. Here's his advice for economical foodies.
广受欢迎的博客"拮据美食家"记录了托尼如何在依靠救济金生活的同时保持对美食的热爱。扣除账单后,托
尼每周有60英镑可以花,其中40英镑用于食物,但10年前他在企业传播领域工作时年薪13万英镑,每周至少
在伦敦最好的餐厅用餐两次。后来他的婚姻破裂,事业崩溃,酗酒问题也变得严重。"社区精神健康团队救了
我的命。当人们对博客反响如此热烈时,我在某种程度上又有了那种感觉。这给了我曾经失去的认可和信
心。但这仍然是需要一天天面对的事情。"现在他住在政府公寓里,正在处理来自文学经纪人的邀约。他感
觉积极向上,但他会继续写博客——不是关于如何尽可能便宜地吃饭——"有那么多人处境更糟糕,几乎没有
钱花在食物上"——而是关于如何在预算有限的情况下吃得好。以下是他给经济型美食爱好者的建议。

filled with leftovers, bread, stock, meat and fish. Planning ahead should eliminate wastage, but if you

店主是你的朋友

knuckles of ham for soups and stews, or beef bones, chicken carcasses and fish heads for stock which,
more often than not, they'll let you have for free.

头,他们通常会免费给你。

Domino's: I know which I'd rather eat.

Directions:
Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
P1 I can pick a date from the past 53 years and know instantly where I was, what happened in the
news and even the day of the week. I've been able to do this since I was four.
P2 I never feel overwhelmed with the amount of information my brain absorbs. My mind seems to
be able to cope and the information is stored away neatly. When I think of a sad memory, I do what
everybody does – try to put it to one side. I don't think it's harder for me just because my memory is
clearer. Powerful memory doesn't make my emotions any more acute or vivid. I can recall the day my
grandfather died and the sadness I felt when we went to the hospital the day before. I also remember

the same way.

P2 我从不觉得大脑所吸收的海量信息会让我招架不住。我的头脑似乎应付得来，各种信息都被整

【衔接】句 1 ↔ 句 2：this 用「这样」承接
句 1 I can pick a date from the past 53 years and know instantly where I was, what
happened in the news and even the day of the week. 已经把能力描述得很完整；句 2 I've
been able to do this since I was four. 用 this 回指整件事。中文成段时，与其在句 2 重复「这种
能力」让句子显得啰嗦，不如用「这样」承接前句——「自四岁起，我就一直能这样」既显化了代
词，又不重复。
句 3 ↔ 句 4：用逗号 + 主动语态把两句并为一句
句 3 I never feel overwhelmed with the amount of information my brain absorbs. 和句 4
My mind seems to be able to cope and the information is stored away neatly. 是「总—分」
关系：前句说「我不被压垮」，后句解释「为什么不被压垮——头脑能应付、信息归置妥当」。中
文成段时用句号断开但语义紧承即可，不必加「因为」「所以」这种生硬关联词，让汉语「意合」
自然流转。
句 5、6、7：「设法搁置→驳斥『更难』→驳斥『情绪放大』」的对照链
When I think of a sad memory, I do what everybody does – try to put it to one side. I don't
think it's harder for me just because my memory is clearer. Powerful memory doesn't make
my emotions any more acute or vivid. 这三句构成「我和大家一样应对悲伤→并不更难→也不更
强烈」的层层递进对照。中文成段时要让这三句的「我并不……」「并不会……」等否定句式呼应，
强化「我虽特别但情感与常人无异」的对照口吻——这是全段的情感主线，不能让三句各自为政。
句 8 ↔ 句 9：「我能记得 A……我也记得 B」的并列加「这两件事」收束
I can recall the day my grandfather died and the sadness I felt when we went to the
hospital the day before. I also remember that the musical play Hair opened on Broadway
on the same day 中 also 是关键衔接词——把「外公去世的悲伤」和「《长发》首演」这两件性
质天差地别的事并列起来。中文里译「我也记得」即可承接 also。最后 they 回指上述两件事，译
作「这两件事就这样以同样的方式涌入我的脑海」收束，把全段「悲喜大小一样自动浮现」的反差

英语二真题(2013)
Section IV Part A
Directions:
Suppose your class is to hold a charity sale for kids in need of help. Write your classmates an email to
1)inform them about the details, and
2)encourage them to participate.
You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET.
Do not use your own name. Use “Li Ming” instead.
Do not write your address. (10 points)

Dear classmates,
I am writing to inform you that our class will hold a charity sale next Saturday, aiming to raise money for
children in need of help. The sale will take place from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. in the school gymnasium. You are
welcome to bring second-hand books, toys and handmade crafts to sell, and all the money we collect will be
donated to these poor kids.
I sincerely hope every one of you can join us. Your participation, no matter how small, will bring warmth and
hope to those children. Let's join hands to make a difference!
Li Ming
